cases.title: Wildcard search
cases.steps: Enter a wildcard query such as *105698*
cases.expected: Results include all awards matching the wildcard pattern
cases.note: Decided: the wildcard behaviour stays as it is, and the guidance that describes it was corrected. The old hint advertised "*text*", the one form that changes nothing - a plain term already matches anywhere in the field, so *105698* and 105698 run the same search. The pages now explain what a wildcard actually buys: 105698* for starts-with, *105698 for ends-with. Shown on Awards and Historical Awards only, because those are the two searches that support it.
cases.environment: dev: UI Amplify job #117 @ bce99fc; API ECS rev 75 (image 20261006T123638Z-8292260); signed-in session, 2026-10-06

progress.deployedBuild: UI Amplify job #117 @ bce99fc (bundle index-DqGd72qq.js); API ECS rev 75 (image 20261006T123638Z-8292260) - unchanged, no API deployment
progress.results: Checked in the browser on the development website. The guidance appears on Awards and Historical Awards and on no other search page - Proposals, Subawards, Negotiations and Global Search carry none, which is correct because those searches do not translate a *. The old "Use *text* for a wildcard search" wording and the "Wildcard (*text*)" and "Partial Award Number" hint chips are gone everywhere. Each form was then run against real archive data and behaves as described: 105698, 105698* and *105698 each returned 2 awards, and on a term where anchoring makes a difference the three forms separated clearly - 00001 returned 15,099 awards, 00001* returned 11, and *00001 returned 15,092. Anchoring demonstrably narrows the search.
progress.limitations: The guidance is deliberately not shown on Proposals, Negotiations, Subawards or Global Search: those searches bind the typed term directly, so a * there is matched as a literal character and finds nothing. That difference between modules is unchanged by this work and is not itself covered by this case.

cases.title: Empty search submission
cases.steps: Submit the search with an empty input field
cases.expected: App shows an appropriate prompt/validation instead of erroring or showing all records
cases.note: Decided: an empty search is a starting state, not an error. Submitting with an empty box and no filters makes no request and shows no records - that was already true - and the page now says "Enter a search term, or apply a filter, to see results." instead of simply doing nothing. Searching with filters alone is supported and unchanged, and Global Search keeps its own two-character minimum.
cases.environment: dev: UI Amplify job #117 @ bce99fc; API ECS rev 75 (image 20261006T123638Z-8292260); signed-in session, 2026-10-06

progress.deployedBuild: UI Amplify job #117 @ bce99fc (bundle index-DqGd72qq.js); API ECS rev 75 (image 20261006T123638Z-8292260) - unchanged, no API deployment
progress.results: Checked in the browser on the development website. With an empty box and no filters the page shows the guidance, fires no search request at all, shows no records and shows no error. Applying a filter alone - no typed text - runs a real search and returned 9,586 awards, so filter-only searching still works. Global Search keeps its own behaviour: a single character answers "Enter at least 2 characters to search." and does not search, while a longer query searched normally. On Historical Awards the guidance carries an extra sentence, because choosing a Versions value on its own does not start a search there; with a search term and Versions set to historical the search ran and returned 30 records.
progress.limitations: The case as written expected a prompt "instead of erroring or showing all records". Neither of those was ever happening - the page made no request and showed nothing - so what was added is the missing acknowledgement, not a new guard. The module API still accepts an empty query and lists everything, paginated; that is deliberate and reachable only by typing a URL, not through the page.

progress.deployedBuild: UI Amplify job #117 @ bce99fc (bundle index-DqGd72qq.js); API ECS rev 75 (image 20261006T123638Z-8292260) - unchanged, no API deployment
progress.results: Checked in the browser on the development website, on a real two-level Award family. Opening a result and then an Award showed the "Back to search results" link alongside the breadcrumb, pointing at the exact search that was run, page number included. Moving up the breadcrumb to the parent Award kept the link pointing at the same search, and so did reloading the page. Clicking it returned to the result list exactly as it had been left. Hand-crafted return targets were refused rather than followed: an off-site address, a protocol-relative one, a javascript: one and one carrying a hidden control character each produced no link at all, while an ordinary internal search address was accepted.
progress.limitations: The return link appears only when the reader actually arrived from a search. Opening a result in a NEW TAB - middle-click, or Cmd/Ctrl-click - and opening a bookmarked or pasted Award address both arrive without that context, and in those cases the link is not shown at all rather than guessing a destination. Both were confirmed on the website. The breadcrumb is unaffected and still appears. This is deliberate: the search is carried in the page's navigation state rather than in the address, which is also why a copied Award link never carries someone else's search terms.

cases.steps: Click Download Award Report on an award detail page
cases.expected: A confirmation prompt appears before download; resulting file is correctly named and not corrupted
cases.note: Decided: no confirmation prompt. The archive is read-only, so a report download is non-destructive and a prompt would prevent nothing; the button instead shows a busy state and cannot be submitted twice. The file itself was checked separately rather than inferred from that busy state - it was opened in a PDF reader, parsed, and representative pages were read.

progress.change: No code change. The decision and the revised criterion are recorded in docs/QA_DECISION_RECORD.md.
progress.deployedBuild: UI Amplify job #115 @ f1ca19d; API ECS rev 75 (image 20261006T123638Z-8292260)
progress.results: Checked in the browser on an Award detail page, signed in. Clicking Download Award Report started the download immediately with no confirmation dialog, and the control showed a busy state while the report was prepared. The downloaded file was then checked on its own terms, because a busy state says a request is in flight and a parsed filename says only that a name was read - neither shows the file is sound. The server supplied the filename itself, and it named the Award the report was opened from. Two independent parsers agreed the document opens cleanly, is not encrypted, and holds 39 pages, and every one of those pages parsed with readable text. The first page, a middle page and the last page were then rendered and read: a cover carrying the Award's own summary fields and the read-only archive notice, a populated interior section whose tables render with their headers and rows intact, and a closing appendix that ends the document cleanly. Page numbering runs 1 to 39 and matches the parsed count, so nothing is truncated.
progress.limitations: One Award and one build. Three of 39 pages were read; the other 36 were confirmed to parse with extractable text but were not read. The downloaded report is held locally as evidence and is not attached here, because it carries real archived award data. A separate, still open audit finding about credentials in this report is unaffected by this case - a limited scan of this one file did not reproduce it, which is not a clearance.

lastObservation.behaviour: A query matching nothing showed “No direct matches” with no results and a “Show 5 related results” action; revealing them produced a Related results section, and a new search hid them again. Suggestions showed real titles.

progress.results: Checked in the browser on the released builds. A nonsense query showed 0 results, “No direct matches” and an explicit “Show 5 related results” action, with nothing related rendered until it was clicked; revealing added a Related results section explaining the suggestions, and running a new search hid them again. A mixed query (pediatric asthma) showed 7 direct results above the Related heading and 3 suggestions below it, with no action needed and no “no direct matches” claim; direct cards carried no Semantic match chip and every suggestion did. Each of five Negotiation suggestions carried its own title and no other card's - Vertex fellowship BU CI, Teaming agreement, evaluation of Abbvie immunology compounds, Potential FFS Engagement - and a Subaward suggestion showed title, sponsor and status (1008, An internet based prospective study of time to pregnancy, NIH/NICHD, 07. Executed). Genuinely empty searches returned nothing at all with no failures. Ordinary and wildcard searches were unaffected, Global Search kept its two-character minimum, and TC-017's control-character handling and TC-018's 200-character limit both still applied. One finding raised during this verification was withdrawn: cards appeared to show a document number instead of a title, which turned out to be an error in how the check read the page rather than anything the page did - the identifier is the card's first line by design and the title renders beneath it. Traced from the browser's own response through to the rendered card; no change was needed.
progress.limitations: Two checks are covered by automated tests only and were not reproduced on this website. A module failing mid-search cannot be triggered from the browser - every malformed input is now refused before it reaches a module - so the behaviour that keeps a failure distinct from “nothing found” is proven by test rather than observation. The fallback that shows a document number when a record has no title is likewise test-proven: only one such Negotiation is known on dev (document number 1120419) and semantic ranking cannot reliably be steered to it.

cases.title: Historical proposal version navigation
cases.steps: In Kuali Documents, search proposal 01394406 and open Document 1000570 (version 2).

cases.note: Confirmed functional defect, reported by Lalitha. Opening document 1000570 (version 2) showed a page headed Version 4 / Workflow 1000951 - the latest version, not the one selected. Cause: a proposal document row carried the proposal NUMBER as its destination, and that address is the family page, which forwards to whichever version is current. Every one of the four documents therefore led to the same page. Fixed in code by sending each row to its own version instead. Award, Negotiation, Subaward and IRB already did this, so only Proposal was affected.

cases.title: Proposal status labelling
cases.steps: Compare the status shown in the Proposals list with the statuses on a proposal detail page.
cases.expected: It is clear which status is being shown and what it means.
cases.note: Usability clarification, reported by Lalitha - the stored statuses are correct and none were changed. The Proposals list showed a bare ACTIVE, which reads as an open or pending proposal. It is actually the sequence status, which says whether a row is the current version. The detail page shows the same record as Sequence status ACTIVE and Status Not Funded, and both are right: version 4 is the current version of a proposal that was not funded. Kuali Documents separately showed Archived for that same version, which is a third thing again - what became of the record. Fixed in code by naming each one: the list value is labelled Sequence status, and the Kuali Documents badge is labelled a Disposition. Board category: this sits under Known issue because the website still showed the confusing label at the last observed deployment, not because any stored value is wrong.
